A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same xKG research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original PaperBench Code-Dev experiments, node ablations, code-quality experiments and human evaluations of graph quality.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds replication scores comparing graph configurations on two additional replication targets in Table 6.

M1.justification: The graph architecture, construction pipeline, verification and agent integration remain unchanged. The xKG+ label denotes the 56-paper graph already described in v2 Appendix B.1; it introduces no new algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds reported agent-replication evaluation on bridging-data-gaps and sample-specific-masks. These papers already served as corpus-expansion targets in v2 Appendix B.1, but v2 reported construction statistics rather than agent-replication evaluation on them. The original five tasks and both graph corpora are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain unchanged. Table 6 reuses BasicAgent/o3-mini with graph configurations; the original versus expanded graph comparison varies corpus size without introducing a new baseline method.

E3.justification: Table 6 adds a controlled comparison holding BasicAgent/o3-mini fixed across no graph, the 42-paper graph and the 56-paper graph. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.1's explicit one-hour limit repeats the setting already stated in v2 Section 3.1.

E4.justification: V3 adds a downstream test of whether graph expansion improves replication on the two expansion targets. V2 demonstrated expansion through corpus statistics only. Existing node ablations, code-quality analyses, human comparisons and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains best@3 reporting, and the code-quality experiment retains three runs per condition and the same boxplots. Table 6 adds no separate run-count, seed or uncertainty information.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports bridging-data-gaps/sample-specific-masks scores of 11.55/24.09 without xKG, 13.93/31.73 with the 42-paper graph, and 44.64/42.47 with the 56-paper graph, all using BasicAgent/o3-mini. These are added results; the previously reported scores and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1's graph equations and node/edge definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds mathematical assumptions, theoretical results or proofs beyond the retained formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: executable knowledge graphs, integration across agent frameworks, replication gains and automatic extensibility. The new appendix experiment supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: The expanded MU-DPO discussion restates the existing explanation involving precise technical details and modular reference code. Appendix B.1 supplies performance evidence for the retained adaptability interpretation. The limitations and Appendix C's failure mechanisms remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 changes 'nitrogen list' to 'filename list' in two reproduced prompt instructions, locally revising implementation documentation. Hyperparameter values, configuration information, construction costs and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning against earlier research are unchanged, including the distinction from ExeKG. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized paragraph revisions in Sections 3.3, A.1 and B.1, adds acknowledgements, shortens prompt subsection headings and corrects wording. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: V3 adds the replication comparison in Table 6 and a domain/subfield breakdown of the retained five tasks in Table 8. Existing appendix tables are reordered and relocated, producing some page reflow. Figures 1–6 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 demonstrated graph expansion through construction statistics; v3 Table 6 adds a controlled check of its downstream replication benefit, strengthening support for practical adaptability. The gain is limited to two tasks with one agent/model configuration and lacks separate uncertainty details. The main method and existing evidence remain intact.
